title: Small models close the gap: three new releases this week
summary: Northwind's Lumen-7, Bluefin's Kestrel Mini and Harbor's Orbit-S all landed this week. Lumen-7 is the standout on reasoning benchmarks; all three numbers are self-reported so far.

content.markdown:
## What happened

Three labs released new small language models this week, and the gap between small and large models kept shrinking. The most notable release, **Lumen-7**, scores within a few points of last year's frontier models on common reasoning benchmarks while running on a single consumer GPU.[^1]

## The releases

- **Lumen-7** (Northwind Labs): 7B parameters, open weights under a permissive licence, 128k context. The lab says it was trained mostly on synthetic data checked by a larger model.[^1]
- **Kestrel Mini** (Bluefin AI): 3B parameters, aimed at phones. It runs fully offline and supports 12 languages, including Japanese.[^2]
- **Orbit-S** (Harbor Research): 12B parameters, tuned for coding. Early users report it handles multi-file edits well but struggles with long test suites.[^3]

## Benchmarks at a glance

The labs' own numbers are summarised in the table below. Independent results are still coming in, and self-reported scores tend to be optimistic, so treat them as a rough guide rather than a ranking.

## What to watch

- Whether independent evaluations confirm the reported scores over the next two weeks.
- Licence details: Lumen-7's licence allows commercial use, while Orbit-S restricts it for companies above a revenue threshold.
- On-device performance: Kestrel Mini's claims about battery use have not been tested by anyone outside the company yet.

[^1]: Northwind Labs announcement.
[^2]: Bluefin AI blog.
[^3]: Harbor Research release notes.
